steps.text: Cook and stir bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until evenly browned. Add onion and sauté until tender. Drain excess oil, if desired.
Stir in baked beans, brown sugar, ketchup, and mustard. Cook, stirring occasionally, until hot and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Baked Beans
raw_recipe.description: These baked beans are quick to make on the stovetop with bacon, onion, brown sugar, ketchup, and canned baked beans for a classic side dish made easy.
raw_recipe.name: Simple Baked Beans

Stir in baked beans, brown sugar, ketchup, and mustard. Cook, stirring occasionally, until hot and bubbly.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is great, however I've made a few modifications that have made it even better! 
1. it's not really necessary to use as much bacon as the recipe calls for. If you cut the bacon in half it still tastes the same, and is not quite as bad for you!
2. always drain the bacon grease before adding the onions, and always drain the sauce from the canned beans before adding them, or the recipe comes out too soupy.
3. I think the mustard taste is a little strong, so I cut back on the mustard just a tad.

I've made this recipe several times for about 20 people, and everyone loved it!

Mmmm, really delicious. I've never really done anything to baked beans before but this really added to them. I cooked the bacon and then removed it and poured out the grease. I then carmelized the onions in the same pan (just a hint of bacon grease in the skillet). Then I added the bacon, beans, ketchup and mustard. I know it seems weird to add ketchup and mustard but it tastes great. I only added about a tablespoon of brown sugar and it was plenty sweet.

I used only 5 slices of bacon, cooking 4 in the microwave and only one, chopped up, in a pan with the chopped onion. I used 2 28-oz. cans of bush's original baked beans. Put in my slow cooker on low for 2 hours. Delicious!

Our family loves baked beans in the summer months! I only used half the bacon specified in the recipe (and it was turkey bacon). Cut the brown sugar in half and added a small amount of cooked ground sage sausage. Instead of cooking in the oven, placed in crock pot and cooked on low for 2 hours. I really like adding leftover hamburgers or meatloaf crumbled up the next day in this.

This recipe really saved me tonight. My husband was grilling pork chops and I was craving baked beans. I easily halved the recipe for just us 2 and used a regular cam of red beans and pure maple syrup as others have done. I made them on the grill in a little cast iron skillet. I will make again!

Like others I modified the recipe just a bit. I sautéed diced 1 cup diced frozen onions in a tiny splash of olive oil. I used a 28-oz can of plain "baked beans" from Wal-Mart. Didn't drain. Added 1/4 pound of bacon crumbles (I'm lazy). 1/4 cup ketchup; 2 tbsp yellow mustard; About 2-3 tbsp brown sugar. Simmer at least 20 minutes for the bacon to soften. I also added about 2 tsp of Kitchen Bouquet just to darken the dish. Totally optional. Tasted fantastic! Definitely adding this to my recipe book.

This is pretty much the recipe I use and that has been a part of my family ever since I can remember. There are some minor changes I make. First, 2 28oz cans of Bush Homestyle beans will make a good amount for a crowd. For my family of 5, just one can will do. I do NOT DRAIN THE CANS!!!!! You will lose flavor! Take out that nasty piece of salt pork or whatever it is. Dump the beans in a crock pot. I don't bother sauteing the onion or cooking the bacon before hand. I just cut up my bacon (1/2 lb for the 2 large cans I mentioned) and onion and put it right in with the beans. I eyeball the ketchup, mustard, and brown sugar, but I know that my ratio is different. If I had to guess, I'd say I probably use about 3/4 cup ketchup for the 2 cans of beans I mentioned earlier, 1 (maybe 2) tablespoons of mustard, and 2 or 3 loose handfuls of brown sugar. Let it cook all day on low. About an hour or so before you want to serve it, give it a taste to see if it needs anything, and if seems soupy, just turn the crock pot up for that last hour. These are the only baked beans I will eat.

I like this recipe because it’s simple. I used only 2 strips of bacon and used all of the fat to cook the onion. Don’t reduce the amount of onion and be sure to cook it until it’s soft. I used half the brown sugar, half the ketchup and only a teaspoon of mustard. I use Bush’s Original Baked Beans and never, ever drain the beans. To me, the onion and the sauce that Bush’s uses for their baked beans is what makes this recipe work. It’s why I was able to reduce the brown sugar, ketchup and mustard. Never, ever drain the sauce from canned baked beans, just never. Yes, you have to cook them longer to reduce the liquid but you are concentrating the excellent flavors the beans were packed in, not tossing them down the drain.

Good recipe. I made a few changes to make this a little lower in calories. I put 2 large cans of vegetarian beans in a crockpot on low heat. I used thin sliced center cut bacon. I then cook the onions before throwing them in with the beans. I used one-carb ketchup and Splenda brown sugar. I used a very little amount of mustard. I added in a pinch of cayenne pepper for a kick. Cooked in slow cooker for about 4 hours. Turned out wonderful. Family didn't know it was low calorie.
Been making this dish w/ Bush Baked beans for over 20yrs. I use browned beef, add bell peppers & no Ketchup nor mustard but add bbq sauce. Let simmer 15/20 minutes & it's a winner!

This recipe was very good and sooo easy as well as fast. I decreased the amount of mustard by half and added a little Lea & Perkins steak sauce. Drained a little of the juice from the canned beans. No other changes. Will definitely be making in the future.
Great, but I added a 1/4 cup of molasses. Personal preference, not really baked beans to me unless it has molasses.

The only thing I did differently (that I did not see in the original recipe), was draining the juices out of the cans of pork beans !!! I read other reviews that stated that it is too runny if you don't drain the juices before adding it to the bacon and onion !!! Truly a DELICIOUS recipe !!! Brought it to a picnic and it was devoured quickly with everyone commenting on how delicious it was !!!!! Thanks for sharing !!!! SOOOO easy to make !!! I will definitely use this again for barbecues and picnics this summer !!!!!
It tasted great! Fast and easy.
I didn't have any brown sugar so I substituted with syrup. The beans were so tasty!
Used Van Camps pork and beans- not as much sauce in these, have used a similar recipe for years.
I added real bacon bits for more bacon flavor yummy!
No it was amazing it’s also my moms recipe thank you
